Suzetrigine targets NAV1.8 sodium channels as a non-opioid pain alternative
recent_posts.summary: Vertex Pharmaceuticals has released suzetrigine, a new class of pain drug that targets the NAV1.8 sodium channel — found exclusively on pain-sensing nerves, not in the brain or heart. Unlike opioids or traditional pain relievers that broadly suppress the nervous system, this drug locks the NAV1.8 channel closed, preventing the electrical signal that transmits pain from ever forming. It is being described as the first true alternative to opioids in decades, with no addiction potential or psychoactive effects.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 makes a full rack one unit of AI compute
recent_posts.summary: Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 redefines the unit of AI compute by packing 72 GPUs and 36 CPUs into a single liquid-cooled rack treated as one machine. The key enabler is NVLink 6, a proprietary interconnect running at 3.6 TB/s per GPU with direct chip-to-chip connectivity across all 72 GPUs simultaneously, eliminating the bottleneck of traditional PCIe buses. Liquid cooling makes the thermal density physically feasible. The result is 3.6 exaflops of compute and claimed 10x inference performance over Blackwell, signaling a shift where the rack — not the chip or server — becomes the fundamental unit of AI compute.

recent_posts.title: Inside NVIDIA's robotics stack at GTC 2026
recent_posts.summary: A firsthand look at NVIDIA's robotics ecosystem from GTC 2026, covering the Jetson Thor compute module, the sim-to-real gap in robot training, and the emerging data flywheel concept borrowed from autonomous vehicles. Includes interviews with NVIDIA's robotics software lead Spencer Huang on world models and CI/CD for robots, and Open Mind founder Jan Liphardt on OM1, an open-source robot OS with an app store. Also covers a ride in a self-driving Mercedes running NVIDIA's drive stack at L2++, with plans for Level 4 robotaxi deployment via an Uber partnership. Key insight: the tools (Isaac, Groot, Cosmos, OM1) are now open and accessible enough that domain experts without robotics PhDs can start building.

recent_posts.title: Apple's 8-year neural engine bet and the case for on-device AI
recent_posts.summary: Apple's Neural Engine has grown from 2 cores in the A11 (2017) to a 16-core engine with GPU-embedded neural accelerators in the M5, representing an 8-year hardware thesis on on-device AI. Apple's vertically integrated stack — from transistors to Core ML — enables unified memory, coordinated workload routing, and private local inference that cloud-only approaches can't match. The gap between what the neural engine can do today and what developers have actually built for it represents a significant opportunity. Qualcomm and Intel are making similar silicon bets, signaling industry-wide conviction that meaningful AI compute belongs on the device, not just in the cloud.

recent_posts.title: ServiceNow autonomous IT as an AI orchestration layer for self-healing systems
recent_posts.summary: A sponsored post promoting ServiceNow's Autonomous IT platform, arguing that enterprise AI tools fail not because of the AI itself but due to lack of context and siloed systems. The pitch centers on ServiceNow acting as an orchestration layer that unifies data, security, and workflows, enabling AI agents to autonomously triage incidents, identify root causes, and trigger remediations before teams are even aware of problems.

recent_posts.title: Adobe Firefly launches custom models for consistent AI image generation
recent_posts.summary: Adobe Firefly has launched custom models that let users upload 10–30 reference images to fine-tune a model around their visual identity in about 30 seconds. The trained model treats the user's style as the default and works across all Firefly model architectures. Adobe has also temporarily removed generation caps, offering unlimited generations until April 22nd.

recent_posts.title: China open-sources Origin Pilot the first publicly available quantum OS
recent_posts.summary: China has open-sourced Origin Pilot, the first publicly available quantum operating system — the low-level software layer that actually runs on quantum hardware, calibrates qubits, and manages hardware resources. Unlike IBM and Google, which only release high-level developer tools (Python-based circuit simulators), Origin Pilot exposes the OS layer itself, allowing universities and labs with real quantum hardware to run, build on, and extend it across three hardware types. The move is framed as a geopolitical strategy: while the US relies on export controls to limit China's access to advanced tech, China is doing the opposite — giving away foundational infrastructure to pull the global research community into its ecosystem and potentially set the default standards for quantum computing worldwide.

recent_posts.title: NVIDIA Quietly Spent $4 Billion on Photonics. The Industry Noticed
recent_posts.summary: NVIDIA has committed $4 billion to photonics manufacturers Lumenum and Coherent, signaling a major infrastructure shift from copper to optical interconnects in AI training clusters. The core argument is that copper wires — not chips — are becoming the binding constraint in next-generation AI systems due to resistive heat, signal loss, and energy-per-bit costs at scale. Silicon photonics addresses these by using light instead of electrons, enabling near-zero resistive heat, no signal degradation over distance, and the ability to carry multiple data streams simultaneously via wavelength division multiplexing. MIT research suggests photonic hardware can reduce energy consumption for matrix multiplication operations by over 90% compared to electronic equivalents. The investment is framed as a strategic infrastructure play, with both Lumenum and Coherent committing to expand US manufacturing capacity. The piece argues that photonic interconnects may be more determinative of AI capability progress from 2025 to 2028 than transformer architecture improvements, and positions understanding this hardware shift as a key differentiator for AI systems architects.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia invests $4 billion in silicon photonics to replace copper GPU interconnects
recent_posts.summary: Nvidia has invested $4 billion in silicon photonics, backing companies Coherent and Luma that produce lasers and optical transceivers. Silicon photonics replaces copper-based electrical data transfer with light pulses, offering faster speeds, lower heat, and significantly better power efficiency — critical for gigawatt-scale AI data centers. Nvidia has secured multi-billion dollar purchase commitments to lock in supply chain advantage. The investment signals a likely move toward photonic interconnects in NVLink 2, the scale-up interconnect linking GPUs within clusters, addressing the core bottleneck in AI infrastructure: inter-GPU data transfer speed.
